host_support: 2 full-featured USB-C laptop inputs; Windows uses DP MST; macOS is supported but not for dual independent MST desktops.
display_capability: Windows: 2 × 4K @ 60Hz. macOS: two outputs can light but mirror rather than extend independently.
switching_method: Panel button; wired remote switch button supported.
keyboard_mouse_channel: Shared keyboard/mouse through USB; directly paired Bluetooth input does not automatically follow KVM switching.
clamshell_support: Yes; AV Access explicitly lists clamshell support.
power_delivery: 60W USB-C charging per connected laptop; both hosts remain powered.
known_non_working_combinations: macOS cannot create two independent extended displays through the C20 MST path; the two monitors also cannot be split one-per-host while USB peripherals are shared.
official_support_evidence: AV Access troubleshooting says MacBook dual displays through this MST path are mirrored rather than independently extended. It also says a 4K display falling to 1080p can depend on the laptop's simultaneous video-stream capability and the monitor port, and recommends lowering resolution/refresh rate when video fails. Source
public_user_report: Two independent qualifying reports document configuration-specific iDock C20 behavior: one reports recurring flicker/artifact and signal dropout across Lenovo Legion S7 15ACH6 and Dell Latitude 5490 paths; the other reports a Dell Latitude 5440 limited to dual 1440p60 while the same dock reaches dual 4K60 on another host. Because the conclusions differ, evidence strength is single, not corroborated.

host_support: USB-C host connection carries DisplayPort video and data; HDMI and DisplayPort inputs are also available.
display_capability: Built-in panel: 1 × 2560 × 1440 @ up to 144Hz; DisplayPort daisy-chain output is supported, with downstream ceiling host-dependent.
display_interfaces: HDMI 2.1, DisplayPort 1.4 DSC input/output, USB-C with DisplayPort support.
keyboard_mouse_channel: Keyboard and mouse share through the built-in USB hub when using KVM.
official_support_evidence: ASUS's product FAQ requires one KVM host to use USB-C with DP Alt Mode; a second host using HDMI or DisplayPort also needs a separate USB upstream cable for keyboard/mouse switching. A video-only second-host cable is therefore not enough for KVM control. Source

host_support: 2 USB-C computers; DisplayLink-certified for Windows, macOS and ChromeOS.
display_capability: 2 × 4K @ 60Hz external displays, including extended dual displays on base Apple M-series MacBooks through DisplayLink.
switching_method: Push button; downloadable hot-key software for Windows and macOS.
peripheral_usb_capability: 2 × USB-A + 1 × USB-C at USB 3.2 Gen 2 10Gbps, plus HID USB at 480Mbps.
power_delivery: USB PD 3.0: 90W to active host and 45W to second host; both charge simultaneously.
official_support_evidence: StarTech's DisplayLink support FAQ and public community reply state that macOS requires DisplayLink Manager plus Screen Recording/accessibility permissions; disabling the permission can make DisplayLink-driven displays disappear. The community case did not confirm 129N and is retained only as general DisplayLink support evidence. Sources
public_user_report: Two independent exact-model reports support the specific conclusion that 129N USB/peripheral connectivity can be lost on Apple Silicon Mac paths; one case also reports simultaneous dual-4K blackout. The older MacBook Pro M3 Screen Recording topic did not identify 129N and no longer counts as model evidence. Do not generalize these reports into a universal 129N defect.

host_support: Thunderbolt hosts and USB-C hosts with DisplayPort Alt Mode; Dell lists Windows 10/11, Ubuntu 20.04+ and ChromeOS M107+.
display_capability: 2 × 4K @ 60Hz on qualifying Thunderbolt/HBR3/DSC combinations; up to four external displays under specific bandwidth/topology conditions.
display_interfaces: 2 × DisplayPort 1.4, HDMI 2.0, MFDP USB-C and Thunderbolt 4 USB-C display paths.
switching_method: Not a KVM; single-host dock, so switching hosts requires reconnecting upstream or a separate switching layer.
keyboard_mouse_channel: Standard USB device path; no dedicated KVM keyboard/mouse channel listed.
peripheral_usb_capability: 3 × USB-A USB 3.2 Gen 1; USB-C Gen 2 data plus Thunderbolt 4 ports on compatible hosts.
power_delivery: Up to 130W to supported Dell systems or 90W to non-Dell systems with the 180W adapter.
known_non_working_combinations: Rear HDMI and MFDP USB-C video paths are muxed and cannot both be used as simultaneous video outputs; non-Thunderbolt hosts lose Thunderbolt features.
official_support_evidence: Dell troubleshooting says monitor count and resolution depend on the host graphics path; with Intel graphics plus the system LCD, only two displays may be supported, while discrete Nvidia/AMD configurations can support three external displays plus the system LCD. Dell also recommends a dock power-cycle sequence for flicker or USB failures. Source
public_user_report: Two independent WD22TB4 reports support the specific conclusion that, in dual-4K setups, reconnect or connection order can change negotiated bandwidth, refresh, and resolution, including 4K60 to 4K30. This is a configuration-sensitive user-reported pattern, not a universal WD22TB4 defect.

host_support: Thunderbolt 4/3, USB4 and USB-C computers; official minimums include macOS 11.4+ and Windows 10 20H2+.
display_capability: Windows / Intel Mac / ChromeOS: up to 2 × 4K @ 60Hz. M1 Pro/Max: up to 2 × 6K @ 60Hz. Original M1: one external display through Thunderbolt.
display_interfaces: DisplayPort 1.4 plus downstream Thunderbolt 4/USB4 display paths.
switching_method: Not a KVM; single-host dock with no host-switch control listed.
keyboard_mouse_channel: Standard USB path; no dedicated KVM keyboard/mouse channel listed.
peripheral_usb_capability: 5 × USB-A 10Gbps and 3 × USB-C 10Gbps, plus Thunderbolt 4 ports.
known_non_working_combinations: Original M1 Macs do not support dual external displays through TS4; USB-C hosts have reduced functionality and 2.5Gb Ethernet is Thunderbolt-host dependent.
official_support_evidence: CalDigit's TS4 support knowledge base documents shared bandwidth groups: many USB ports share the same 10Gbps USB hub, while DisplayPort and downstream Thunderbolt ports share the same 40Gbps Thunderbolt bandwidth. High-bandwidth peripherals therefore compete within those groups rather than receiving dedicated bandwidth. Source
public_user_report: One qualifying report documents a successful M3 MacBook Air plus two Samsung M7 4K60 configuration. Two independent high-bandwidth dual-display reports support the narrower conclusion that DSC, Thunderbolt lanes, adapter path, and refresh rate affect the result.

host_support: USB-C with DisplayPort Alt Mode, USB4 or Thunderbolt; Windows 10/11, macOS 11+ and ChromeOS 100+. Full display capability uses DisplayLink software.
display_capability: Up to 3 × 4K @ 60Hz with a DP 1.4 host path; Display 2 and 3 use DisplayLink at up to 4K @ 60Hz each. DP 1.2 can limit Display 1 to 4K @ 30Hz.
display_interfaces: 3 HDMI/DisplayPort output pairs; choose one connector from each display pair.
switching_method: Not a KVM; single-host dock with no host-switch control listed.
keyboard_mouse_channel: Standard USB path; no dedicated KVM keyboard/mouse channel listed.
power_delivery: Current hardware revision: up to 100W USB-C PD; older units with the same model number may be the earlier 60W revision.
known_non_working_combinations: Plugable does not recommend this DisplayLink dock for Linux, gaming or graphics-heavy work; Lenovo ThinkPad P16 Gen 2 is listed as a currently incompatible/limited host combination.
official_support_evidence: Plugable's official product/support page lists the Lenovo ThinkPad P16 Gen 2 (21FA) as an incompatible or limited host: rear TB4 ports expose USB data but not Display 1, while the left USB-C port exposes Display 1 but not USB device connectivity. The unlinked phrase 'some users report' is official support guidance, not a traceable public user report. Source
public_user_report: Three independent qualifying reports cover different conclusions: a successful HP ZBook 14u G6 three-display split across DP Alt Mode and DisplayLink, an MSI GE76 second-display failure, and a 2021 M1 Pro MacBook Pro disconnect case resolved after Plugable's full reset and original USB cable guidance, followed by three stable days and a solved/locked thread. Different conclusions mean single, not corroborated.

host_support: Requires Thunderbolt 4. Anker lists M1 Pro/Max support and excludes base M1/M2 MacBooks and ASUS laptops with AMD CPUs.
display_capability: Windows supports 2 × 4K @ 60Hz and additional higher-count combinations subject to host limits; macOS topology depends on the Mac chip.
display_interfaces: 1 × HDMI 2.1, 2 × DisplayPort and a downstream Thunderbolt display path.
switching_method: Not a KVM; single-host dock with no host-switch control listed.
keyboard_mouse_channel: Standard USB path; no dedicated KVM keyboard/mouse channel listed.
power_delivery: USB PD 3.0 up to 100W; when both 30W USB-C charging ports are used, Anker states laptop output can fall to 65W.
known_non_working_combinations: Not compatible with base M1/M2 MacBooks or ASUS laptops using AMD CPUs.
official_support_evidence: Anker's exact-model FAQ says the host must support Thunderbolt 4, the dock is not compatible with base M1/M2 MacBooks, and laptop charging can fall from the advertised 100W maximum to 65W when both 30W USB-C charging ports are used. Source
public_user_report: Two independent qualifying Apple Silicon Mac reports support intermittent external-display blackout or flicker with Anker 778: an M1 Pro case across HDMI and DisplayPort paths, and an M2 Max / Sequoia 15.1 case with a dual-display Thunderbolt topology. Preserve OS, output path, display count, and host-chip variables.

host_support: Thunderbolt 4/3, USB4 and full-function USB-C hosts; Windows 10+ and macOS 11.4+ are listed, with reduced display capability on some hosts.
display_capability: Windows and supported Intel/Pro/Max Macs: up to 2 × 4K @ 60Hz. Base M1/M2/M3 Macs: 1 × 4K @ 60Hz. Full-function USB-C: one display.
display_interfaces: DisplayPort 1.4 plus 2 × downstream Thunderbolt 4 display-capable ports.
switching_method: Not a KVM; single-host dock with no host-switch control listed.
keyboard_mouse_channel: Standard USB path; no dedicated KVM keyboard/mouse channel listed.
peripheral_usb_capability: 1 × USB-C 10Gbps; 2 × USB-A 10Gbps; 2 × USB-A 5Gbps, plus Thunderbolt 4 data ports.
power_delivery: Up to 90W laptop charging from the included 180W power supply.
known_non_working_combinations: Full-function USB-C hosts support only one display; UGREEN also lists the 2018 Intel Mac mini as incompatible.
official_support_evidence: UGREEN's exact-model compatibility notes say full-function USB-C hosts support only one external display, base M1/M2/M3 Macs support a single 4K@60Hz display, Intel Mac mini 2018 is not compatible, and the dock must be connected to power to function. Source
public_user_report: Three independent reports cover different conclusions: host-port A/B behavior; SSD and 4K-display Thunderbolt bandwidth sharing; and direct-vs-dock exclusionary evidence that removes the dock as the cause of a Surface Laptop 7 4K30 result. Reported 1440p180 is a user-reported observation only; official DisplayResolutionMax remains 8K@30 / 4K@120 / 2K@144 and the main table is unchanged.
